items.title: ICE Has Quietly Changed Its Deadly-Force Rule
items.description: I CE quietly enacted new rules this month that will keep officers involved in deadly-force incidents—such as firing a gun and using a choke hold—off the streets until the completion of an investigation. Previously, these officers were able to return to their regular job in as few as three days. Now they must remain on desk duty until they are cleared by investigators, according to two senior ICE officials with knowledge of the change, who spoke with me on the condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to discuss agency matters with reporters. Under the old rules, ICE supervisors could lengthen an officer’s period of leave, but such an extension was often viewed internally as signaling a lack of confidence in the officer and their version of events. At ICE and other law-enforcement agencies, officers are typically eager to return to full patrol duties as quickly as possible, and not remain in limbo as an investigation plays out. The change, which has not been publicly announced, means that officers who fire their guns, choke someone, or use some other form of deadly force—even if no one is killed—will potentially be limited to performing administrative duties for much longer periods. Acting ICE Director David Venturella and other senior ICE leaders ordered the change late last month, the two senior officials said. ICE and the Department of Homeland Security did not respond to my questions about why the policy change was made or how many such incidents have occurred since President Trump returned to office. ICE officers have shot at least 16 people since last January, four of them fatally, according to public records. Last month, there were two fatal shootings during traffic stops: On July 7, ICE officers in Texas killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old contractor from Mexico, and six days later, an officer in Maine fatally shot Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, a 25-year-old Colombian immigrant. DHS said the officers fired in self-defense, but the incidents are under federal investigation. Veteran ICE officials have worried for months about the competence of the thousands of new recruits who were added during a hiring binge last fall, many of whom were rushed onto the streets after taking a fast-track training course. The ICE officer in Maine, David Brouillette, was a new hire, and his relatives told reporters he had a history of mental-health issues and violent behavior that should have disqualified him from getting a badge and gun. [ Read: The secretary of homeland ] Violent confrontations during traffic stops particularly concern ICE leaders; the agency has not typically had so many officers pulling over vehicles and attempting to arrest people who are in cars. After the shootings last month, ICE and DHS pledged to expedite the deployment of body-worn cameras for ICE officers. Although most of the cameras have been delivered, the officials told me that they don’t know when all of ICE’s roughly 15,000 deportation officers will be wearing them. After the killing in Maine, Venturella and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin halted the use of nonemergency traffic stops—but Trump reversed the directive when immigration hard-liners said it made the White House look weak. The president has said that ICE officers “make mistakes sometimes” and can be “too rough,” but they’re doing a “GREAT job.” A rrests by ICE totaled nearly 50,000 in July, the highest level in a single month since Trump returned to office, the officials told me. The agency is no longer using a city-by-city approach to surge arrests, as it did last year under then–Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem , and this has led to fewer clashes with protesters. But officers remain under pressure to maximize arrests and deportations, and new videos continue to emerge showing officers tackling immigrants and pointing guns at people who are filming them or are allegedly disobeying their orders. ICE leaders say they’re looking for ways to reduce the use of deadly force by giving officers more nonlethal tools. The agency is planning to spend up to $20 million on electrified gloves that allow officers to deliver painful shocks. The gloves, which have been used by some police departments and public-school security officers, will be assigned to ICE teams involved in traffic stops and other potential confrontations, according to the officials I spoke with. They told me the shocks delivered through the gloves are painful but less intense and more localized than those from a Taser, and will be easier to direct than chemical sprays. Prior to the current Trump administration, the use of deadly force by ICE deportation officers in U.S. cities was more rare than shootings by U.S. agents along the Mexico border were, Scott Shuchart, an attorney and a former ICE official who worked at the agency’s Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties from 2010 to 2018, told me. The U.S. Border Patrol reduced its annual number of shooting incidents more than a decade ago by hiring independent consultants who recommended giving agents more nonlethal tools and better training. The number of Border Patrol’s firearm-use incidents, measured across fiscal years, fell from 55 in 2012 to eight last year. Shuchart said the administrative-leave extension “seemed like a healthy signal” that ICE leaders knew “they might have a real problem” after the shooting in Maine . “They don’t want to be creating more risk by putting people back out on the street,” he said. [ Read: ‘Maybe DHS was a bad idea’ ] Deborah Fleischaker, a senior ICE official during part of President Biden’s term, told me that the change to ICE’s rules will matter little if internal oversight mechanisms don’t hold officers accountable for wrongdoing. Trump officials gutted offices at DHS that had reviewed complaints against ICE personnel and about poor detention-center conditions. “If the goal is to ensure that people are on administrative leave through the entirety of an investigation, that’s a good goal, but it doesn’t speak to the quality of the investigation,” Fleischaker said. Fleischaker, now an immigration-policy adviser at the Hispanic-advocacy group UnidosUS, said Trump officials have conveyed a clear message to the federal workforce that “mass deportation is a high-profile goal of this administration and people need to be real careful of getting in the way of anything that slows that down.” In October, Stephen Miller said on Fox News that ICE officers had “federal immunity” to perform their duties while carrying out Trump’s immigration crackdown. But since then, Democratic leaders in several states have vowed to bring charges against ICE officers for use of excessive force. In Minnesota, state prosecutors charged the ICE officer Christian Castro with four counts of second-degree assault and one count of falsely reporting a crime for his role in the nonfatal shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant on January 14—a day after DHS published a clip of Miller’s “immunity” remarks. Minnesota has been seeking Castro’s arrest and extradition from Texas, but Governor Greg Abbott, a Republican, is challenging the request in federal court. CNN reported today that the Department of Justice is considering filing federal charges against Castro.

items.title: Private security firms acting as political militias risk licence revocation, prosecution – National Security Coordinator
items.description: National Security Coordinator COP Osman Abdul-Razak has warned that private security companies and informal community security groups that operate as political task forces or private militias during election periods risk losing their licences and facing criminal prosecution. He said no private entity would be allowed to assume the coercive powers of state security agencies or perform functions reserved for the state. COP Abdul-Razak gave the warning at a national policy dialogue on the Vigilantism and Related Offences Act, 2019 (Act 999), organised by Election Watch Ghana at the Kofi Annan International Peacekeeping Training Centre (KAIPTC). The forum brought together security commanders, legal experts and civil society representatives to discuss the enforcement of the law and measures to prevent political vigilantism. COP Abdul-Razak acknowledged the legitimate role of private security companies and traditional leaders in maintaining community safety but stressed that their activities must remain within the limits of the law. “Community participation must strengthen lawful state authority, not substitute for it,” he said. He warned that private security companies operating outside the terms of their licences could have their authorisation revoked, while individuals involved in prohibited activities could face prosecution under Act 999. “Private security companies operate under specific licences and regulations. Where these operational boundaries are breached, those licences will be lawfully revoked, and perpetrators will face the full rigour of Act 999,” he said. His warning comes amid concerns that political parties could disguise illegal vigilante groups as private protection units, protocol teams or licensed security details ahead of major political events. COP Abdul-Razak stressed that the responsibility for providing security during elections rests with state security agencies operating under the established legal framework. He said the Police-led National Election Security Task Force was responsible for protecting ballot boxes, candidates, electoral officers and the general public during elections. He cautioned that individuals who attempt to exercise unauthorised security powers, particularly by wearing military-style uniforms, carrying weapons or asserting illegal authority, could face arrest and prosecution under Act 999. The National Security Coordinator urged all political actors, private security providers and community groups to respect the law and avoid activities that could undermine Ghana’s electoral security and democratic processes.

items.title: C’River Governorship: PDP candidate accepts Otu debate challenge
items.description: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Cross River, Arthur Archibong, has accepted Gov. Bassey Otu’s challenge to an open debate. Archibong said he was ready to debate Otu at any time and venue the governor chose, provided Otu attended personally. The candidate spoke with journalists in Calabar on Tuesday, responding to a challenge issued by the state Commissioner for Information, Ekpenyong Cobham. “I am willing to honour the challenge to a debate, on one condition: that Gov. Bassey Otu will be there in person. “The people deserve to hear directly from those seeking to lead them, not from proxies,” he said. Archibong said he would not engage Cobham in a war of words, describing the commissioner as his brother and stressing he was not on the ballot. “Pastor Cobham is my brother. But he is not on the ballot, so I will not join issues with him,” he said. Cobham had earlier challenged Archibong to publicly debate the Otu administration’s policies, programmes and performance ahead of the 2027 election. Archibong also defended Arthur Jarvis University (AJU), which he founded in Akpabuyo Local Government Area, against recent criticisms. He described the allegations against the institution as politically motivated, saying AJU was established to contribute to Cross River’s development. He urged critics to focus instead on environmental sanitation, blocked drainages and emergency response, particularly the condition of Watt Market. He said: “Instead of chasing imaginary bedbugs in Akpabuyo, they should come and see the real crisis in Watt Market. “Go there today and see the filth, the stench, the blocked drainages, and traders selling beside refuse.” Archibong also alleged that inadequate resources were undermining emergency response, particularly the state fire service. “Our firefighters have no diesel. Our fire trucks have no water. And when infernos like the one at SPAR Mall happened, we are left helpless,” he said. The PDP candidate expressed sympathy for traders, workers and families affected by the recent fire at SPAR Shopping Mall in Calabar. He promised that his administration, if elected, would strengthen emergency response and provide firefighters with water, diesel and essential equipment. Archibong also questioned the economic benefits of the administration’s foreign investment trips and Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs). “After so many MoUs, show me how many have translated to successful projects that are addressing the pitiful situation of this state. “Where are the factories? Where are the jobs? Where is the relief for the ordinary man?” he asked. The candidate criticised what he described as Otu’s absence during crises, citing recent landslides and the SPAR Mall fire. “When landslides claimed lives and destroyed properties, and when fire swept through our businesses like the recent SPAR Mall crisis, the presence of our governor is nowhere to be found,” he said. On scholarships, Archibong said educational support remained a personal commitment rather than an instrument for political advantage. “Scholarships are a personal act of service. I will not bring charity to the marketplace just to score cheap political points,” he said. He urged voters to make the 2027 election a contest based on ideas, records, competence and service rather than money, intimidation or violence. Archibong said: “Cross River deserves a governor who will not govern from a distance or by proxy. “Our people deserve leadership that shows up, listens and delivers. Let this contest be about ideas, about track records, and about who is ready to serve.” The post C’River Governorship: PDP candidate accepts Otu debate challenge appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Antoine Semenyo makes history as first Ghanaian named in PFA Team of the Year
items.description: Antoine Semenyo has made history by becoming the first Ghanaian player to be named in the PFA Premier League Team of the Year. The Manchester City forward was included in the prestigious XI at the annual PFA Awards ceremony on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, following an impressive 2025/26 campaign. Semenyo is joined in the star-studded lineup by five Arsenal players, four Manchester City players, Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and Brentford striker Igor Thiago. Arsenal’s David Raya, Jurriën Timber, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhães and Declan Rice all made the team after helping the Gunners enjoy the league’s best defensive record, conceding just 27 goals. Manchester City are represented by Nico O’Reilly, Rayan Cherki, Erling Haaland and Semenyo. Fernandes completes the midfield after breaking the Premier League assist record with 21 assists, while Thiago earns his place after scoring 22 league goals for Brentford. Semenyo’s selection represents a landmark moment for Ghanaian football, making him the first player to earn a place in the PFA Premier League Team of the Year. The recognition caps a remarkable period for the forward following his move to Manchester City and underlines his growing status among the Premier League’s elite players. There was also recognition for O’Reilly, who was named the PFA Young Player of the Year after a breakthrough season with Manchester City.

items.title: One killed, 3 injured as gunman opens fire at Kano ‘DJ’ wedding ceremony
items.description: Kano State Police Command has confirmed that one person was killed while three others sustained injuries after a man allegedly opened fire during a marriage ceremony, popularly known as a “DJ” event. The Command’s Public Relations Officer (PPRO), CSP Abdullahi Haruna-Kiyawa, said the incident occurred at Tudun Yola on Aug. 16. He said the police had arrested a 34-year-old man, Rabiu Mukhtar, in connection with the alleged offence. The PPRO further stated that the suspect allegedly used a pump-action gun to shoot four people who sustained injuries. He added that the police recovered the gun from the suspect’s possession. Haruna-Kiyawa said the victims were rushed to Murtala Muhammad Specialist Hospital, Kano, for medical treatment. He identified the victims as Sadiq Abubakar, Umar Rabiu, Muhammad Sadisu and Aliyu Mustapha. According to him, one of the victims, Aliyu Mustapha, later died in the hospital, while the remaining three are responding to treatment. The PPRO further revealed that Mukhtar and one other person were apprehended and taken into custody for investigation at the Command Headquarters, Bompai, Kano. He explained that preliminary information indicated the incident was triggered by music that some people did not like. Haruna-Kiyawa further stated that the suspect told the police he opened fire after he heard that thugs, ‘Yan daba’ were coming to the venue. He said the suspects would be prosecuted after the investigation was completed. The post One killed, 3 injured as gunman opens fire at Kano ‘DJ’ wedding ceremony appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Détroit d’Ormuz : Trump annonce la fin du déminage et menace l’Iran
items.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé mardi que le détroit d’Ormuz avait été entièrement déminé, tout en adressant une mise en garde directe à l’Iran contre toute nouvelle tentative de miner cette importante voie maritime. Dans un message publié sur son réseau social Truth Social, Donald Trump a affirmé avoir été informé par la marine américaine que toutes les mines avaient été retirées ou détruites dans les eaux internationales du détroit d’Ormuz. Il a également prévenu que tout navire qui placerait de nouvelles mines dans le passage maritime serait « immédiatement et systématiquement détruit ». Le président américain a par ailleurs indiqué que Washington continuait de surveiller le détroit, notamment grâce aux moyens de la Force spatiale américaine. Cette annonce intervient alors que le détroit d’Ormuz demeure au cœur des tensions entre Washington et Téhéran. Ce passage stratégique, situé entre l’Iran et Oman, voit habituellement transiter près de 20 % des hydrocarbures mondiaux, ce qui lui confère une importance majeure pour les marchés énergétiques internationaux. Parallèlement, Oman et l’Iran travaillent sur une solution visant à sécuriser progressivement la navigation dans cette zone. Le ministre omanais des Affaires étrangères s’est entretenu mardi à Téhéran avec son homologue iranien afin de discuter d’un « cadre par étapes », comprenant notamment la création d’un corridor maritime temporaire et un projet conjoint de déminage. Selon le communiqué omanais, les deux pays doivent poursuivre leurs discussions techniques afin de parvenir à une solution permanente permettant de garantir la sécurité de la navigation. La situation reste toutefois fragile. Téhéran affirme que le détroit restera verrouillé tant que les États-Unis n’auront pas respecté les engagements prévus dans le protocole d’accord conclu le 17 juin, notamment concernant la levée du blocus imposé aux ports iraniens. De son côté, Washington avait annoncé en juin une mission destinée à faciliter la circulation des pétroliers dans le détroit, notamment grâce à leur escorte par des moyens américains. L’annonce de Donald Trump sur le déminage intervient donc dans un contexte où les initiatives américaines et omanaises se chevauchent, tandis que l’Iran maintient ses exigences. La sécurisation durable du détroit dépendra désormais de l’évolution des négociations entre les différentes parties. The post Détroit d’Ormuz : Trump annonce la fin du déminage et menace l’Iran appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Agrobusiness, sécurité alimentaire : À Niamone, la terre veut retenir ses enfants
items.description: À Tobor, la terre produit, forme et prépare une nouvelle génération d’entrepreneurs agricoles. Dans cette commune du département de Bignona, tous misent sur les terres disponibles, l’eau d’Affiniam et la formation agroécologique pour faire de l’agriculture un rempart contre l’exode vers l’Europe. ZIGUINCHOR- À peine franchi le portail du centre agroécologique de Tobor, le regard est happé par une scène inhabituelle. Ici, la terre semble devenir un lieu d’apprentissage, d’expérimentation et d’espoir. Des parcelles verdoyantes s’étendent dans l’enceinte du centre. Des plants sont bien entretenus. Plus loin, des jeunes habillés en t-shirts verts s’affairent autour de nouvelles pousses qu’ils mettent en terre avec application. À quelques mètres, d’autres découvrent les métiers liés aux énergies renouvelables, dont le solaire, tandis que l’aquaculture ouvre de nouvelles perspectives. Le centre agroécologique est ainsi devenu un point de convergence pour une jeunesse venue de Niamone, mais aussi de plusieurs régions du pays. Certains apprenants ont même fait le déplacement depuis Goudiry. Tous partagent une même ambition : apprendre, produire et, surtout, pouvoir vivre de leur savoir-faire. Dans ce décor, les mains plongent dans la terre pendant que les esprits se forment. Pour Atab Badji, maire de Niamone, sa commune possède une réserve foncière nécessaire pour franchir ce cap. « Niamone dispose d’un potentiel foncier important, contrairement à Bignona et Ziguinchor. Nous sommes également situés à une position stratégique, à proximité des marchés gambien et bissau-guinéen. Et nous avons également la chance de disposer d’un centre de formation agroécologique », se glorifie l’élu territorial lors de la visite du ministre de l’Agriculture, Dr Cheikhou Oumar Bâ. Mais l’argument le plus fort, selon lui, se trouve dans les salles et les parcelles du centre. Les jeunes qui y sont formés. « Nous avons ici des jeunes qui peuvent devenir de véritables fermiers. Ils n’ont aucune raison d’aller chercher leur avenir en Europe. Ils disposent d’un centre agroécologique moderne, avec de bonnes conditions de formation et d’hébergement. Il nous appartient maintenant de les accompagner et de leur donner les moyens de réussir », insiste Atab Badji. Affiniam, le réservoir qui peut changer la donne À Niamone, la question foncière ne constitue pas le seul motif d’espoir. L’eau pourrait également jouer un rôle déterminant dans la transformation agricole de la commune. Pour cela, le maire pointe le potentiel du barrage d’Affiniam, récemment réhabilité. Une ressource qu’il considère comme un levier encore sous-exploité. « Notre commune compte onze villages et dispose de nombreuses potentialités. Nous ne sommes pas confrontés à un problème majeur d’accès à l’eau, grâce au barrage d’Affiniam. Il y reste encore environ 25 millions de mètres cubes d’eau non exploités qui pourraient contribuer fortement à notre objectif d’autosuffisance alimentaire », se réjouit Atab Badji. Pour l’édile, le plus difficile a déjà été réalisé avec la réhabilitation de l’ouvrage. Il faut désormais franchir l’étape suivante : amener l’eau jusqu’aux terres agricoles. « Le barrage a été réhabilité à coups de milliards. Il faut maintenant réaliser les investissements nécessaires pour connecter les champs au réseau d’eau. Une telle démarche permettrait de sécuriser la production et de donner aux agriculteurs les moyens de travailler dans de meilleures conditions », estime Atab Badji. Des terres disponibles, une réserve d’eau importante, une situation géographique avantageuse et une jeunesse en formation, etc. L’équation est donc résolue. Il ne manque, selon le maire, qu’un ingrédient essentiel : l’investissement. « Les investisseurs qui cherchent une destination agricole doivent regarder du côté de Niamone. Investir ici, c’est exploiter un potentiel économique considérable, mais c’est aussi offrir une alternative à l’exode des jeunes vers l’Europe et vers d’autres destinations », plaide-t-il. Cette volonté de faire de la jeunesse un acteur du développement local ne date toutefois pas d’hier. Dès son arrivée à la tête de la commune, Atab Badji a lancé le projet « Un village, une vallée, une ASC, un champ ». L’ambition est de faire des Associations sportives et culturelles (ASC) un véritable outil de mobilisation agricole. Dans les parcelles du centre agroécologique, les jeunes continuent de planter. Geste après geste, ils mettent en terre bien plus que de simples plants. Ils y matérialisent leur ambition de construire leur avenir ici, plutôt que de le chercher ailleurs. À Niamone, la bataille contre l’exode des jeunes pourrait ainsi commencer par une chose aussi simple qu’un geste de la main : planter, cultiver et récolter sur sa propre terre. Par Gaustin DIATTA (Correspondant)

items.title: «Un effacement d'une partie de l'histoire»: en Guinée, la destruction de la Maison centrale de Conakry a commencé
items.description: À Conakry, une page de l’histoire carcérale du pays est en train de se tourner. La Maison centrale de Conakry, dans la commune de Kaloum, est progressivement démolie depuis le samedi 22 août. D'abord inaugurée en 1903 - tandis que le bâtiment en cours de destruction date, lui, de 1933 - cette prison était devenue au fil des décennies l’un des lieux les plus emblématiques du système pénitentiaire guinéen. Après l'indépendance, elle a vu passer nombre d'acteurs politiques de premier plan, comme les ex-présidents Alpha Condé, Moussa Dadis Camara, ou encore le journaliste Souleymane Diallo. Frédéric Le Marcis, anthropologue à l'École normale supérieure de Lyon, revient sur l'histoire de cette prison et son usage politique pendant la période coloniale et après l'indépendance de 1958.

items.title: Mahama calls for responsive healthcare regulation to improve patient safety
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has called for a more responsive healthcare regulatory system to improve patient safety and protect public trust in healthcare delivery. The President made the call at the 28th Annual Conference of the Association of Medical Councils of Africa in Accra on August 24. The conference brought together health regulators and other key stakeholders from across the continent under the theme, “ Responsive Regulation for Safer Communities towards Universal Health Coverage .” Africa’s healthcare systems are facing growing pressure from population growth, changing disease patterns and increasing demand for quality care. President Mahama said these challenges make responsive and adaptive regulation critical to ensuring patient safety and strengthening healthcare delivery. He also called for greater collaboration among African countries to train more healthcare professionals and ensure a fairer distribution of the continent’s medical workforce. The Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, who was also present, outlined the government’s plans to decentralise specialist training and expand healthcare services to underserved areas. He said the measures form part of efforts to make quality healthcare more accessible to people across the country. Stakeholders at the conference believe stronger regulation, deeper collaboration among African countries and expanded specialist training will be critical to improving patient safety and advancing Universal Health Coverage across the continent.

items.title: El tenis celebra el retorno de Carlos Alcaraz, el gran deseado
items.description: No siempre se tiene la oportunidad de jugar al lado de una leyenda, así que Carlos Alcaraz, de nuevo en acción, lo saborea, se divierte y aprende. Al alegrón por su reaparición y una vez abandonada la penumbra a la que obliga un contratiempo de larga duración, se añade esta última experiencia y la foto a guardar: así es, yo jugué con ella. Es un simple bolo , puro entretenimiento, pero su compañera se lo toma muy en serio. Así que él obedece, se aplica y toma nota; ahora bien, predomina la contención, o así lo expresa su servicio: ninguno supera los 185 km/h. Por tanto, difícil extraer cualquier conclusión; si acaso, la respuesta favorable de la muñeca lastimada. La noche se resuelve con una remontada frente a Lloyd Glasspool y Erin Routliffe (5-3 y 4-1, en 58 minutos), y la derrota posterior contra Flavio Cobolli y Belinda Bencic (5-4(7) y 4-1, en 55 minutos). Seguir leyendo Y DE PROPINA, LA MAGIA DE FEDERER Por si Alcaraz y Serena no fueran alicientes suficientes, la jornada contó también con la intervención de Roger Federer. El genio suizo, de 45 años y retirado desde hace cuatro, con 20 grandes y un sello sin igual, participó en una doble exhibición tras haber asistido en julio a Wimbledon. Primero rindió a Andy Roddick — el último campeón local en el terreno masculino — y posteriormente disfrutó de la compañía de John McEnroe, con el propio Roddick y Andre Agassi al otro lado de la red. Este último se refiere a Alcaraz en el documental de Novak Djokovic (El Lobo en Invierno). “Djokovic, Federer y Nadal jugaron este deporte de maneras muy diferentes y todos fueron geniales a su manera. Y ahora hay jugadores, en concreto Alcaraz, que juega como Djokovic, Federer y Nadal cuando quiere... El tenis sigue mejorando”, desliza el norteamericano. Federer, por su parte, asegura que no se plantea ni por asomo un hipotético regreso al circuito (“mi cuerpo ya no da para más”) y también elogia al murciano, con el que nunca se midió: “Me gustaría jugar contra él, es emocionante verle y nunca pude hacerlo. Por suerte, ya no tengo que preocuparme por ello…”.

items.title: IERPP accuses GoldBod of breaching transparency law, says quarterly trading reports removed from website
items.description: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) is facing fresh pressure over transparency after the policy think tank, the Institute of Economic Research and Public Policy (IERPP), alleged that its quarterly trading reports have been removed from its website. In a statement issued on Monday, August 25, 2026, the IERPP demanded urgent answers from GoldBod, citing Section 42 of the Ghana Gold Board Act, 2025 (Act 1140), which requires the Board to publish quarterly reports on its operations, revenue, contracts, expenditure and responsible sourcing. The IERPP said the reported removal of the reports from the website raises concerns about compliance with the law establishing GoldBod. “Section 42(2) requires GoldBod to ensure access to those reports. The law does not merely require GoldBod to upload reports; it requires meaningful public access to them,” the IERPP said in the statement signed by its Executive Director, Prof. Isaac Boadi. The institute stressed that it was not alleging wrongdoing, but said the reported disappearance of the reports raised “legitimate questions”, given GoldBod’s role in managing Ghana’s strategic gold reserves and its significant public financial interests. The IERPP is demanding that GoldBod explain who authorised the removal of the reports, when it occurred and why. It also wants the Board to publish both the original and revised versions of any reports in which figures have been corrected or replaced, together with explanations of all material changes. “The timing of the trading report publication is particularly important because it sits at the centre of a growing question: what is the actual financial relationship between GoldBod, the Bank of Ghana, and the wider gold-purchasing programme?” the statement said. IERPP’s six demands The IERPP has made six demands of GoldBod, including: Restore all previously published quarterly reports and establish a permanent public archive. Explain any deletion, withdrawal, amendment or replacement of reports. Publish original and revised versions where figures have changed, together with reasons for the changes. Provide the publication and removal dates for each report. Ensure full disclosure under Section 42, including information on revenue, contracts, expenditure, operations and traceability, remains publicly accessible. Disclose off-taker fees, trading margins, discounts, assay charges and other transaction costs for independent scrutiny. The IERPP argued that GoldBod could not demand compliance and reporting from licensed gold buyers while making its own legally mandated reports difficult to access. “Where public resources and national gold are involved, citizens must be able to understand the transactions, prices, contracts, fees, discounts, trading margins and ultimately who bore the risks and costs,” the statement said. The think tank also warned against allowing GoldBod to “become a black box”, noting that gold is one of Ghana’s important sources of foreign exchange and that the Board’s activities have implications for exports, reserves, the Bank of Ghana and public finances. “Public gold requires public scrutiny. Public money requires public accountability,” the IERPP said. It added that Section 42 was enacted specifically “for the purpose of transparency and accountability” and argued that the obligation should not be treated as a temporary website exercise.

items.title: Future of Energy Conference: Africa cannot industrialise in the dark – ECOWAS Bank President
items.description: President of the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID), Dr George Nana Agyekum Donkor, has warned that Africa’s industrialisation ambitions will remain elusive without adequate, reliable and affordable energy. He said Africa had for decades supplied the world with raw materials, including cocoa, gold and bauxite, while importing finished products at significantly higher costs, a situation that has constrained value addition, job creation and economic transformation on the continent. “We have lit up other continents while over 600 million of our own people remain in darkness,” he stated as the keynote speaker at the Future of Energy Conference 2026 in Accra. “Africa cannot industrialise in the dark”. Dr Donkor said achieving Africa’s industrialisation agenda would require deliberate policymaking, stronger coordination and substantial investment in energy infrastructure. He stressed that no industrial revolution could take off without a robust and dependable energy system capable of supporting manufacturing and other productive sectors. According to the African Development Bank (AfDB), Africa requires about $25 billion annually to achieve universal access to electricity, highlighting the scale of investment needed to close the continent’s energy deficit. Dr Donkor said EBID, recognising energy as central to Africa’s industrialisation, had committed more than $1 billion of its resources across the energy value chain as of June 2026. “We have invested in electricity generation, both conventional and renewable, transmission and distribution projects, while also supporting fuel procurement to keep economies running,” said Dr Donkor. He said the bank’s Growth, Resilience and Optimisation Strategy would see it commit a minimum of $2 billion to the energy sector by 2030. Dr Donkor proposed a four-pronged approach to addressing Africa’s energy deficit and creating the foundation for industrialisation. The approach includes strengthening national and regional grid systems, deploying large-scale renewable energy systems, exploiting domestic natural gas resources and expanding embedded generation capacity within industries. “Effective industrialisation in Africa requires a mixed energy system consisting of reliable electricity, renewable energy, natural gas, regional power pools and distributed energy solutions. The objective is not merely to increase electricity access but to ensure that industries receive affordable, reliable and sufficient energy to drive manufacturing, value addition, employment creation and economic transformation,” he said. From minerals to industrial value chains The Africa Mineral Development Centre (AMDC) also underscored the need for Africa to move beyond the extraction and export of raw minerals and develop industries capable of converting its vast natural resources into higher-value products. Interim Director-General of the AMDC, Claudine Sigam, said Africa already possessed many of the mineral resources required to participate meaningfully in the global energy transition. She said the key challenge was to develop the energy, industrial capacity, skills and markets required to transform those resources into materials, competitive enterprises, jobs and sustainable prosperity. “When the global conversation focuses on minerals, Africa must broaden into materials, value chains and markets. Minerals alone does not create industrialization. We need competitive energy to transform minerals into materials, industrial capabilities to transform materials into products, and markets capable of sustaining those industries,” she said. Ms Sigam said Africa’s energy, mineral and industrial transformation should therefore be treated as an integrated development agenda aimed at maximising value creation on the continent. The Future of Energy Conference 2026 is being held in Accra on the theme: “Powering Africa’s Industrial Transformation: Energy Systems for Value Addition and Competitiveness”.

items.title: C’River 2027: PDP guber candidate accepts Otu’s debate challenge
items.description: …Says poll not about money bags, but scorecard , performance By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Cross River, Sir Arthur Javis-Archibong, has accepted a challenge to engage Gov. Bassey Otu in an open debate ahead of the 2027 governorship election. Archibong, who spoke with journalists in Calabar on Tuesday, said he was ready to participate in the debate at any time and venue chosen by the governor, provided Otu would attend personally. His response followed a challenge issued by the state Commissioner for Information, Pst Ekpenyong Cobham. “I am willing to honour the challenge to a debate, on one condition: that Governor Bassey Otu will be there in person. “The people deserve to hear directly from those seeking to lead them, not from proxies,” he said. Archibong said he would not engage in a verbal exchange with Cobham, describing the commissioner as his brother. “Pastor Cobham is my brother. But he is not on the ballot, so I will not join issues with him,” he said. The PDP candidate also defended Arthur Jarvis University (AJU), the private university he established in Akpabuyo Local Government Area, against recent criticisms. Archibong said the institution was established to contribute to the development of Cross River and would not be distracted by what he described as false allegations. “All sorts of things have been said about AJU. Funnily enough, the last I heard of bed bugs was in my childhood when we slept on straw beds,” he said. He challenged those criticising the university to demonstrate their own contributions to the state, particularly through employment and business development. “Before pointing fingers at AJU, they should first point to one business they own where they have employed at least 15 people from this state,” he said. Archibong said attention should instead be directed at pressing challenges confronting the state, including environmental sanitation, drainage and emergency response. “Instead of chasing imaginary bedbugs in Akpabuyo, they should come and see the real crisis in Watt Market. “Go there today and see the filth, the stench, the blocked drainages, and traders selling beside refuse. That is the environmental emergency staring us in the face. “Our firefighters have no diesel. Our fire trucks have no water. And when infernos like the one at SPAR Mall happened, we are left helpless. “That is where government attention should be, not in spreading lies about a university that is trying to add value,” he said. On scholarships, Archibong said supporting education had always been a personal commitment and should not be reduced to political propaganda. “Scholarships are a personal act of service. I will not bring charity to the marketplace just to score cheap political points,” he said. He urged Cobham to conduct proper research before making public statements, particularly by consulting residents of Akpabuyo, Bakassi and other communities who, he said, had benefited from his interventions over the years. Archibong also criticised what he described as attacks on his character, urging the commissioner to uphold the values associated with the Christian faith. “Barefaced lying is alien to the calling of a pastor. If he is truly a pastor and not self-acclaimed, then he should be wary of the God who sees and knows all things,” he said. He added that the 2027 election should be determined by the electorate rather than money, intimidation or violence. According to him, This election will not be won by attacking institutions that should be supported by government. Arthur Jarvis University is a thriving institution that employs our people and trains our children. “Instead of support, it is being subjected to unprovoked attacks simply because of politics. That is not how you build a state.” Archibong further criticised the Otu administration over what he described as the governor’s absence during moments of crisis, citing landslides and the recent fire incident at SPAR Shopping Mall in Calabar. “When landslides claimed lives and destroyed properties, and when fire swept through our businesses like the recent SPAR Mall crisis, the presence of our governor is nowhere to be found,” he said. He questioned the economic impact of the administration’s foreign investment trips and memoranda of understanding (MoUs), saying Cross Riverians were yet to see sufficient tangible outcomes. “Government keeps going out for MoUs, but Cross Riverians are yet to see the dividends. “After so many MoUs, show me how many have translated to successful projects that are addressing the pitiful situation of this state. “Where are the factories? Where are the jobs? Where is the relief for the ordinary man? You cannot be absent at home in the name of chasing investors abroad, while the house is on fire and there is no water to put it out,” he said. The PDP candidate expressed sympathy for traders, workers and families affected by the early Saturday fire at SPAR Shopping Mall. “My heart bleeds for every trader, every young worker, and every family whose livelihood went up in flames that morning. “As a businessman myself, I know the pain of watching years of sweat and sacrifice turn to ashes overnight,” he said. Archibong promised that, if elected, his administration would strengthen emergency response and equip the state fire service with the necessary resources. “Under my watch, we will never be caught unprepared again. Emergency response will be fast, equipped, and present. “We will ensure our fire service has water, has diesel, and has the tools to protect lives and properties within the time of need. No Cross Riverian should ever have to face disaster alone,” he said. Archibong said leadership was ultimately about presence, service and accountability. “Cross River deserves a governor who will not govern from a distance or by proxy. “Our people deserve leadership that shows up, listens, and delivers. That is the covenant I offer the people of Cross River in 2027. “Let this contest be about ideas, about track records, and about who is ready to serve and nothing less,” he added. items.title: The Transcendence of Dolly Parton
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. Dolly Parton transcended. It almost didn’t matter what: class, gender, region, musical genre, partisanship. She transcended boundaries in all of them. During an era when politicians act like pop stars, pop stars are expected to engage in politics, and politics divide fiercely, Parton was perhaps the only person in the United States who commanded nearly universal affection. Her death today, at 80, leaves an absence that no contemporary cultural figure could dream of filling. Parton’s origin story was, in the most literal sense, a rags-to-riches tale. She was born in a one-room cabin in the Appalachian Mountains of East Tennessee, one of 12 children of an illiterate sharecropper father. She memorialized her impoverished childhood in “Coat of Many Colors,” which tells of how her mother sewed a jacket from rags. When she wears it to school, “with patches on my britches / and holes in both my shoes,” her classmates mock and laugh at her. Rather than a hard-luck story, this is a triumph. Parton gets the last laugh: “But they didn’t understand it and I tried to make them see / That one is only poor only if they choose to be.” The song showcases one of the keys to Parton’s success: the ability to bare her soul while keeping a sense of humor and a smile. Her rise to fame began when she was hired by the rhinestone-adorned country singer Porter Wagoner as a “girl singer” in his act. Parton quickly demonstrated that she had more than an attractive face and voice, writing a string of successful songs, such as “Jolene” and “My Tennessee Mountain Home.” One indication of her songwriting talent was that her most famous song was a bigger hit for another singer. Parton had initially hoped that Elvis Presley would record “I Will Always Love You,” but she refused his manager’s demand to give Presley songwriting credit, and she cut the song herself. It topped the country charts twice, but after Whitney Houston rerecorded the song for The Bodyguard ’s soundtrack in 1992, it was a No. 1 pop hit for weeks. The country singers and collaborators Porter Wagoner and Dolly Parton pose for a portrait with their backup band, the Wagonmasters, circa 1968. Wagoner is wearing a Nudie Suit designed by Nudie Cohn of Nudie’s Rodeo Tailors. (Michael Ochs Archives / Getty) Today, little separation exists between country music and the mainstream, but the genre garnered much less respect when Parton’s career began. She helped tear down old prejudices in an era when many music listeners might have professed to like “anything other than country.” Her success helped pave a path for later crossover stars such as Shania Twain and Taylor Swift. She pursued her own genre experimentation, too, collaborating with a range of artists. When she was nominated for the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2022, she protested that she wasn’t a rock musician and tried to withdraw from consideration. When the hall refused, she announced with appealing humility that she would earn the honor by making a rock album—her 49th and final—with guests including Joan Jett, Ringo Starr, and Paul McCartney. Parton always maintained her connection to rural southern music. Few country stars could claim a more authentic origin. She kept her down-home accent and platinum-bouffant hairstyle, and she spoke openly about her abiding Christian faith. These traits may have allowed her to take stands that might otherwise have been controversial. (She also avoided electoral politics, and declined Presidential Medals of Freedom from both Donald Trump and Joe Biden.) Like her predecessor Loretta Lynn, she cultivated a no-nonsense strain of feminism in her lyrics. In 1980, she starred alongside the outspoken liberals Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin in the movie 9 to 5 , a workplace comedy in which three women conspire to get even with their sexist-pig boss. Parton agreed to take the role if she could write the theme song, and the track has proved even more enduring than the film. “It’s a rich man’s game no matter what they call it / And you spend your life puttin’ money in his wallet,” she sang. Was this working-class grievance or progressive economics? Radical feminism or mass-market entertainment? Why not both? From left : the American actors Jane Fonda, Dolly Parton, and Lily Tomlin on the set of the film 9 to 5 , directed by Colin Higgins, in Los Angeles in 1979 (Steve Schapiro / Corbis / Getty) Parton was beloved by the gay community, and she reciprocated that affection . She also quietly fostered change using her fortune. In 1986, she opened Dollywood in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, and the theme park became the largest job provider in the area. In 1995, she launched Dolly’s Imagination Library. Starting first in her native Sevier County, and then expanding around the United States as well as in a few other countries, the program mails a book each month to children from birth to age 5, to encourage literacy and a love of reading. In 2020, she donated $1 million to help fund the development of a COVID-19 vaccine, then proudly received the shot. In her middle age, during a perhaps less enlightened time in American society, Parton was often a punch line. Her voluptuous chest and many plastic surgeries were frequent fodder for jokes, and Parton perfected the trick of playing along with the gags while also subverting them. One of her earliest singles is titled “Dumb Blonde,” but it warns, “This dumb blonde ain’t nobody’s fool.” In a 2002 New York Times interview, she said, “Hopefully people can see beneath the hair to know there’s a brain, beneath the boobs to know there’s a heart, and behind all the other stuff to know there’s some talent.” If that wasn’t always the case, Parton got her wish in the end. Admiration for her became an unshakable conviction across cultural lines. One sign of Parton’s status is that even Trump is on his best behavior, treating her death with a reverence he usually reserves only for his biggest public admirers, of whom she was not one. The president ordered flags flown at half-staff for a week to mark her death. It is a fitting farewell for an artist who united Americans in a way that few people ever have or will. Logging In Was Never Supposed to Be This Complicated By Will Oremus One afternoon earlier this month, I pulled up to the rec center and realized that I had a problem. It was not the three boisterous tweens in the back seat who were clamoring to be set loose in the basketball gym. It was my parking app. I had somehow gotten logged out of Passport Parking, which has become the only way to pay for a spot in much of my town, and it was demanding a four-digit PIN to let me back in. My first guess drew a warning message in red letters: “Invalid PIN. PIN cannot contain 4 sequential numbers, 2 repeated digits, or the last 4 digits of your phone number.” I searched my trusty password manager, which was supposed to spare me these predicaments, but it came up empty. By that point, the kids had run ahead and piled themselves against the gym door, waiting for me to let them in. Lately, the process of accessing apps and websites has grown dizzying. “I’m in password hell,” a colleague confided to me recently. Read the full article. items.title: L’œil de Guinéenews : une des réalités insolites que nous offre la circulation urbaine
items.description: Nous sommes à la T10, peu après 15 heures. Il tombe une fine pluie intermittente. Pour ceux qui connaissent la zone, un grand rond-point a été aménagé à cet endroit, ces derniers temps. Pour mieux dispatcher la circulation et aussi, embellir la capitale, n’est-ce pas ? Mais, voilà que, malgré la visibilité qui était assez bonne, un semi-remorque plate-forme, transportant du ciment, bâché et roulant vers Kagbelen, vient s’encastrer en plein, sur le flanc du rond-point. Seule la hauteur de la maçonnerie l’a freiné, l’empêchant d’escalader l’ouvrage en béton pour passer de l’autre côté de la route. C’était assez surprenant et spectaculaire. On entendait les témoins des faits dire, tout autour : ‘’ quelle chance les usagers ont eu de ne pas avoir croisé ce camion dans ce rond-point ! ’’ Sous réserve des conclusions du commissariat de la routière qui coiffe la zone, nous pouvons estimer que le chauffeur étant venu tout droit sur le rond-point a eu, soit un problème de maîtrise ou d’inattention ou alors, c’est un ennui technique lié aux freins qui s’est produit. Toujours est-il qu’il y a eu un cumul de dangers. D’abord, un gros risque pour les usagers, doublé de la destruction de l’infrastructure routière. En plus, une forte perturbation de la circulation. Les usagers (automobilistes et motocyclistes) ont tous été obligés de circuler à gauche, avec les risques que cela comporte. Pendant ce temps, le convoyeur du camion a rapidement fait transborder le ciment dans une autre remorque, cette fois, un camion ridelle, bâché. Peut-être a-t-il pensé à l’éventuelle pluie pouvant tomber à tout moment.

items.title: Terrorists now use social media, remittance platforms to raise funds — Bukarti
items.description: By Juliet Umeh Security analyst and lawyer, Dr Bulama Bukarti, has said that terrorist groups operating in Nigeria are exploiting social media, international remittance services to raise and move funds into the country. Bukarti, who spoke on Channels Television on Tuesday, said terrorism financing was becoming more sophisticated, warning that unsuspecting Nigerians at home and abroad could unknowingly fund terrorist activities. He said the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit, NFIU, report revealed how foreign-based individuals solicit donations through Telegram and Instagram, disguising appeals as humanitarian or educational support. According to him, donations ranging from $50 to $500 are accumulated in a master account before being broken into smaller amounts and transferred to different recipients in Nigeria through international remittance platforms. “These people are doing all of this in order to evade Nigeria’s tightening financial regulations,” he said. Bukarti urged Nigerians to conduct checks before donating online, stressing that the warning was not against genuine humanitarian assistance. “It is not a call for us to stop supporting humanitarian or educational appeals. It is a call for us to do our due diligence, know the person you are donating to and make sure you trust them,” he said. He also called for stronger linkage of Bank Verification Numbers, BVN, with SIM cards, saying deceased persons’ accounts and accounts controlled by third parties had allegedly been exploited for terrorism financing. “We need to strengthen the linkage between Bank Verification Numbers and SIM cards. The NFIU and the Nigerian Communications Commission must work together to ensure that only properly registered and verified SIM cards are linked to bank accounts and used for financial transactions. “The only way to defeat terrorism is to follow the money,” he said. He also warned: “People need to be careful. If someone says, ‘carry this for me’, trust them first and make sure you know what you are carrying,” he said. On jungle justice, Bukarti said, “Jungle justice is not justice. It is injustice, and it is cruel, and it only sends a country into anarchy.” He called for prompt investigations and prosecutions, saying law-enforcement failures did not justify mob action. “The failure by government or security and law enforcement agencies doesn’t justify jungle justice,” he said. Bukarti also called for a multinational security pact between Nigeria, Niger and Benin to tackle emerging terrorist corridors. “Nigeria needs to do more,” he said, adding that cutting terrorists’ financial lifelines was crucial. items.title: La date du premier forum de la diaspora mauritanienne fixée à fin octobre
items.description: Le ministère des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Mauritaniens de l'extérieur a annoncé la date de la première édition du Forum des communautés mauritaniennes de l'étranger. Dans un communiqué publié ce mardi, le ministère a indiqué que le forum se tiendra les 29, 30 et 31 octobre 2026 à Nouakchott, sous le haut patronage du président mauritanien Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani. Il a ajouté que la fixation de la date du forum venait couronner un vaste processus de consultation, qui a notamment donné lieu à des rencontres directes avec les communautés mauritaniennes dans 22 pays répartis sur quatre continents, avec la participation de représentants d’associations et de fédérations, d’experts scientifiques et professionnels, d’hommes d’affaires et de personnes intéressées par les questions relatives aux Mauritaniens de l’extérieur. Le ministère a souligné que les résultats de ce processus ont été débattus lors d’une journée de réflexion qu’il a organisée le 30 juin dernier, avec la participation de secteurs gouvernementaux, de parlementaires et de représentants d’organisations communautaires. Les discussions ont permis d’identifier les principales revendications et préoccupations soulevées par les communautés et de les transmettre aux instances compétentes pour qu’elles soient étudiées et traitées. Selon le ministère, ce forum constitue un espace national fédérateur de dialogue et de concertation entre les pouvoirs publics et les communautés mauritaniennes dans différents pays du monde, permettant ainsi de discuter de leurs aspirations et des défis auxquels elles sont confrontées, et d’étudier des solutions et des mécanismes concrets pour améliorer leur situation et renforcer leurs liens avec la mère patrie. L’ordre du jour du forum comprend des axes portant sur le développement des politiques et du cadre institutionnel régissant les affaires des communautés, le renforcement de la protection sociale et juridique des Mauritaniens à l’extérieur, ainsi que la mise à profit des compétences et de l’expertise mauritaniennes à l’étranger pour le transfert de connaissances et le soutien au développement. Le ministère a affirmé qu’il s’efforcerait, en coordination avec les secteurs gouvernementaux et les partenaires nationaux et internationaux, de garantir une participation large et équilibrée reflétant la diversité géographique, professionnelle et sociale des communautés mauritaniennes à l’étranger.

items.title: 𝗙𝗚 commences reconstruction of Carter Bridge
items.description: . Project to gulp 𝗡548.98𝗯𝗻, ready within 24 months By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Federal Government has commenced the demolition of the dilapidated Carter Bridge in Lagos, with an estimated N548.98 billion set for reconstruction. The rehabilitation project is expected to be completed within 24 months instead of the 36 months initially scheduled for the project. Minister of Works, Sen. Dave Umahi, disclosed this while inspecting the reconstruction of the Carter Bridge and the Iddo Bridge in Lagos. The minister was accompanied by the Minister of State for Works, Sen. Mohammed Goronyo, and some members of the National Assembly, including the Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Works, Mr Akin Alabi. Umahi said the Federal Government was accelerating work on the bridge because of its importance to vehicle movement in Lagos. He said the bridge, which is about 1.58km long, had remained in use for more than 60 years with inadequate maintenance, leading to serious structural problems. “Carter Bridge has stayed for over 60 to 70 years with no maintenance. “The lifespan of every bridge is about 50 years, and what we found out from the underwater survey is that a lot of the piles had detached from the pile caps. “It is like having the leg removed from the hip. There was also a lot of rust within the piles, while scouring and illegal sand mining contributed to the failure of the bridge,” he said. The minister said the government had completed the new design for the bridge and introduced features that would improve traffic flow and protect the structure from future damage. According to Umahi, the new bridge will have additional ramps to reduce congestion, with one carriageway built above the other. He said a cable-stayed section would also be introduced to provide adequate clearance for navigation. “We are going to be flying one carriageway over the other, increasing the number of ramps to decongest traffic towards the ramp sections. “We are also having a cable bridge to contain the 105 spans for navigational activities. It is going to be beautiful,” Umahi said. He said the contractor, China Civil Engineering Construction Company (CCECC), had completed about 15 per cent of preparatory work, including acquiring the project yard and constructing access roads. According to the minister, piling is expected to commence before the end of the week. The minister said the government was also introducing additional protective measures, including gabions, to protect the bridge foundations from erosion and scouring. Umahi said that Carter Bridge could not be closed completely during the reconstruction because of its importance to vehicular movement. He said the Federal Government would therefore carry out regular monitoring and maintenance of the existing structure until the new bridge is completed. “If we close Carter Bridge, Lagos will go into katakata (chaos). That is why we are maintaining it while the reconstruction is going on,” he said. Umahi also said the Federal Government was applying similar measures on the Third Mainland Bridge, adding that the intervention was designed to extend its lifespan by another 50 years. He expressed confidence that the new Carter Bridge would last for more than 100 years because of the additional engineering features being introduced. The minister commended the contractor for progress made so far, and thanked members of the National Assembly for their support. Earlier, the Federal Controller of Works in Lagos, Mr Olufemi Dare, told the minister that the contractor had mobilised to site and was constructing access roads. He said the contractor’s yard had also been established, while piling work was expected to begin soon. Dare also briefed the minister on progress on the Iddo Bridge. He said three spans of the bridge — spans 13, 14 and 15 — had failed completely and had been replaced. “Three days ago, we completed the casting, and the bridge has also been elevated, giving us very good headroom underneath. “In another 10 days, after the concrete has cured, we will open this section to traffic and close the other section, after which demolition will start immediately,” he said. Dare said that other components of the Iddo Bridge project were also progressing, with drainage and Continuously Reinforced Concrete Pavement (CRCP) works about 90 per cent completed. He expressed confidence that the Iddo Bridge intervention would be completed within two months. Sen. Allwell Onyesoh, who was in the minister’s entourage, described the reconstruction of Carter Bridge as timely, noting that Lagos had experienced significant population growth since the bridge was originally constructed. Onyesoh said the National Assembly would support measures necessary to complete the project successfully. The Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Works, Mr Akin Alabi, said the reconstruction was long overdue. He said that the bridge ought to have been rehabilitated and expanded many years ago. He commended Umahi for his commitment to the project, and expressed confidence that its completion would benefit Lagos residents and Nigerians generally. items.title: Industrie du gaming : le Maroc ouvre son fonds d’innovation aux entreprises du jeu vidéo
items.description: Le gouvernement marocain franchit une nouvelle étape dans le développement de l’industrie du jeu vidéo. Le ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce a lancé, dans le cadre du programme d’appui à l’innovation 2026-2028, un dispositif spécialement consacré au secteur du Gaming. L’objectif est d’identifier et de sélectionner les projets les plus prometteurs afin de leur permettre de bénéficier du Fonds de soutien à l’innovation (FSI), faisant ainsi du jeu vidéo l’un des nouveaux secteurs pouvant accéder aux mécanismes publics de financement de l’innovation. Le programme prévoit notamment une aide au prototypage, couvrant jusqu’à 70 % du coût du projet, avec un plafond fixé à 1 million de dirhams par projet. Ce volet cible les initiatives portant sur le développement de produits et de solutions innovantes dans l’industrie du jeu vidéo. Un second dispositif concerne la phase pilote de fabrication. Dans ce cas, la contribution de l’État peut atteindre 30 % du coût du projet, avec un plafond de 3 millions de dirhams. Cette aide vise à accompagner les entreprises lors du passage du développement à la production expérimentale. L’intégration du gaming au dispositif intervient dans le cadre de la nouvelle version du Fonds de soutien à l’innovation, qui couvre la période 2026-2028. Un avenant à la convention relative au FSI a notamment élargi la liste des entreprises pouvant bénéficier de ces mécanismes aux acteurs de l’industrie du jeu vidéo. Plusieurs institutions participent à ce dispositif, notamment le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances, le ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce, le ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication, l’Agence nationale pour la promotion de la petite et moyenne entreprise ainsi que la CGEM. À travers cette initiative, les autorités marocaines souhaitent également valoriser le potentiel humain du pays. Le ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce met notamment en avant le vivier de jeunes talents marocains, avec l’ambition de faire du Royaume un hub africain de l’industrie du jeu vidéo. Cette nouvelle mesure s’inscrit dans une stratégie plus large. En 2024, le ministère de la Jeunesse, de la Culture et de la Communication avait lancé une plateforme dédiée à l’industrie marocaine du jeu vidéo, destinée notamment aux développeurs, startups et investisseurs. En mars 2026, une deuxième édition du programme « Incubateur Gaming » a également été lancée au profit de 12 entrepreneurs marocains du secteur, en partenariat avec l’ambassade de France au Maroc. Le gouvernement prévoit par ailleurs la création d’une « Cité de l’industrie du jeu vidéo à Rabat », ainsi que le développement de programmes de formation et d’incubation, de nouveaux mécanismes de financement et l’organisation du Salon marocain de l’industrie du jeu vidéo. Avec l’ouverture du FSI au gaming, le Maroc entend ainsi accompagner les entreprises du secteur depuis la conception de leurs prototypes jusqu’à la phase de production expérimentale, tout en renforçant son ambition de devenir une plateforme régionale de référence dans cette industrie technologique. The post Industrie du gaming : le Maroc ouvre son fonds d’innovation aux entreprises du jeu vidéo appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Help comes to Alajo as DirectAid brings relief items to flood victims
items.description: Relief has reached residents of Alajo in Accra who were affected by the June 2026 floods, following the distribution of food and household items by humanitarian organisation DirectAid. The distribution, held on Tuesday, August 25, is part of a wider relief programme expected to support about 1,500 families in five communities affected by the floods. The programme, estimated at about GH¢2 million, will also cover residents of Alogboshie, Kasoa, Nana Krom and Abeka, with the exercise expected to be completed next week. At Alajo, beneficiaries received packages containing bags of rice, six litres of cooking oil, 10 packs of spaghetti, beans, tomatoes and other food items. The organisation also distributed household essentials, including mattresses, bedsheets, blankets, towels and cleaning products such as soap and Parazone. Sami Henedak Ahmed, Country Director of DirectAid The Country Director of DirectAid, Sami Henedak Ahmed, said the intervention was aimed at supporting families whose livelihoods and homes were affected by the June floods. He said the relief items were provided through the support of DirectAid’s donors in Kuwait, with assistance from government officials involved in coordinating the exercise. The organisation also plans to extend support to clinics and hospitals, where medical supplies and other items will be donated to assist their operations. Joy among beneficiaries The distribution was met with visible excitement among beneficiaries, many of whom wore broad smiles as they received the items. Some beneficiaries enthusiastically shouted praises and expressed gratitude to DirectAid and its donors, as the relief packages were handed out. For families still dealing with the effects of the floods, the assistance provides food and household essentials at a time when many are struggling to rebuild their lives. DirectAid said the intervention was a gesture of solidarity from its donors in Kuwait to affected families in Ghana. The organisation expressed appreciation to the donors and government officials who supported the exercise and helped facilitate the distribution. The remaining distributions in Alogboshie- Wednesday, Kasoa- Thursday, Nana Krom- Saturday, are expected to take place before the programme ends next week with a final distribution at Abeka- next Tuesday. The late June floods cost a lot lives and destroyed property worth millions. Read also: June 29 floods killed 39, affected nearly 92,000 people – Muntaka

items.title: “Somebody created the loss” – Haruna Mohammed backs Minority’s call for GoldBod probe
items.description: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has backed the Minority in Parliament’s demand for answers over GH¢22 billion losses linked to Ghana’s gold trading operations, insisting that the matter requires a full investigation. NPP Deputy General Secretary Haruna Mohammed said the party believes the available reports point to GoldBod as the source of the costs and losses, despite the Ghana Gold Board’s position that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) report did not directly attribute the losses to its operations. Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story on Tuesday, August 25, Mr Mohammed said the relevant reports must be examined carefully to determine where the losses originated. He argued that although the Bank of Ghana’s accounts may reflect the losses, the institution responsible for gold trading under the current legal framework is GoldBod. Read also: Minority files fresh motion seeking parliamentary probe into reported $1.7bn GoldBod loss “Lawfully, in this country, now, as we sit, it is GoldBod that is in charge of buying and selling of golds. And those particular losses that have happened, whether accounting losses or transaction losses, is going to be related to the body that has been responsible for that.” Mr Mohammed questioned why costs arising from gold trading activities should be reflected as a burden on the Bank of Ghana and called for clarity on how the losses were incurred. “If such a cost has been occasioned, and per the laws and the guidelines that have been put in, the loss is attributed to the Bank of Ghana, but in each wise sense, somebody created the loss. So we should be interested in who created the loss.” He said a closer examination of the Bank of Ghana’s records would provide information on the source and accumulation of the costs. According to him, the NPP’s position is based on its interpretation of the available information, which it believes points to GoldBod. “And when you go and read it very carefully, you realize that it is coming from GoldBod. And if it is coming from GoldBod, as citizens of Ghana, we have the right to question why such an institution is always running us into losses.” Mr Mohammed said the Minority’s call for an investigation was therefore justified, adding that the NPP would fully support the parliamentary effort to establish what caused the losses. Read also: NPP backs Afenyo-Markin’s push for answers over alleged GoldBod losses “We have the right to question. And that is why the Members of Parliament have questioned that. And the party is coming out to back the Members of Parliament in the fullest time for investigation to be conducted into that, so that we will be able to get to the bottom of the matter.” GoldBod has maintained that the IMF report cited in the debate did not directly attribute the reported losses to the operations of the state-owned gold trading institution. The NPP, however, insists that the relevant financial records should be examined to establish where the losses originated and who should be held responsible.
